title: General Science
intro: General Science is the biggest GA scorer after Polity, and it draws straight from school NCERT — Physics, Chemistry and Biology basics plus everyday applications. SSC asks definitions, units, one-line formulae and 'which is which' facts (vitamins, gases, instruments). You do not need deep theory; you need the clean, memorised fact. This chapter packs the highest-frequency items by subject.

topics.name: Physics Basics
topics.details: Know the SI units and basic laws: force is measured in newtons (N), energy in joules (J), power in watts (W). Newton's second law gives Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma). The speed of light is about 3 × 10⁸ m/s; sound is far slower (~343 m/s in air).

topics.name: Chemistry Basics
topics.details: Matter is made of atoms; an element has one kind of atom, a compound two or more chemically combined. Water is H₂O, common salt is NaCl, and CO₂ turns lime water milky. Acids have pH below 7, bases above 7, neutral = 7.

topics.name: Biology & Human Body
topics.details: The cell is the basic unit of life; the mitochondrion is its 'powerhouse'. Humans have 206 bones and the heart has four chambers. Blood group O is the universal donor and AB the universal recipient.

topics.name: Science in Everyday Life
topics.details: Everyday science links principles to daily observations: lightning is seen before thunder because light is faster than sound; a pressure cooker cooks faster because higher pressure raises water's boiling point.

solved.problem: Why is lightning seen before thunder is heard?
solved.solution: Light travels much faster than sound.

solved.problem: Why does a pressure cooker cook food faster?
solved.solution: Higher pressure raises water's boiling point.

solved.problem: Which vitamin is made by the skin in sunlight?
LPG mainly consists of which gases?

unsolved.problem: We hear thunder after lightning because light is ___ than sound.
A pressure cooker raises the ___ point of water.

shortcuts: Memorise SI units (force N, energy J, power W) and one-line laws (F = ma).
Vitamin deficiencies: C → scurvy, D → rickets, A → night blindness.
Universal donor O, universal recipient AB; 206 bones; heart 4 chambers.
Air ≈ 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen; CO₂ turns lime water milky.
mistakes: Confusing universal donor (O) with universal recipient (AB).
Saying oxygen is the most abundant gas in air — it is nitrogen.
Forgetting power is in watts, not joules.
pyq: SSC packs in 6–9 science items per Tier 1 — units, vitamins, blood groups, gases, and everyday-life "why" questions. Clean one-line facts from NCERT are exactly what is asked.

summary: General Science is one-line NCERT recall across Physics (units, F = ma), Chemistry (H₂O, NaCl, pH, air composition) and Biology (cell, 206 bones, blood groups, vitamins), plus everyday "why" questions. Memorise the clean facts and units — they are exactly what SSC asks, and there are many marks here.
